issues.reason: The `Degree` level slot takes "the surface adverb, lemmatized" as a bare symbol (`very`, `slightly`, `excessive`); double-quoted string literals belong to `Name` / `QuantifierPhrase` / `CardinalityPhrase`, so `"almost"` there is ill-typed.

`Degree` keeps the positive precisely because "intensifiers entail the property", but "almost simultaneous" denies full simultaneity, so `(Member sk_raid_group_1 simultaneous)` asserts what the text stops short of.

gaps_confirmed: approximators ("almost", "nearly", "virtually") on an adjective — `Degree` is defined for intensifiers/downtoners that entail the positive, and nothing carries a modifier that cancels it

a distributed part-whole between two groups ("the bodies of seven of the bombers") — `PartOf` is defined for a component of an object or a member of a group, not for a group of parts standing against another group
new_gaps: whether `Degree` may carry a property-cancelling approximator with the positive atom withheld — the `forKind` comparison-class case is the only precedent for a `Degree` atom without its positive, and it is not stated to generalize
repair_summary: Removed the over-asserted `(Member sk_raid_group_1 simultaneous)`. Rewrote `(Degree sk_raid_group_1 simultaneous "almost")` as `(Degree sk_raid_group_1 simultaneous almost)` — the level as a bare lemmatized surface adverb, the positive withheld on the `forKind` precedent, which records what the text says without entailing simultaneity.
notes: Simultaneity is a property of the collection itself, so keeping it on the raid-group symbol (rather than distributing) is right and was left alone. The partitive, the sealed report with its definite groups projected, the suppressed past-perfect ordering and "Friday night" are unchanged.
